solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Male model, topless, reversing partiality

indicators.note: reversing tells us the whole string built from the first three pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to model for an artist is to sit
topless clothing leaves the chest open

explanation.surface: A male model posing without a top and being shown favouritism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' reads as describing the model, but it is a synonym piece, and 'reversing' turns the whole string round.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring one's relatives or friends with jobs is a classic form of partiality or bias.

clue.text: Occasionally in boat his fly's broadcast

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of the phrase is taken

explanation.surface: An angler in a boat casts a fly from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' picks the even letters of 'in boat his fly's': N, O, T, I, F, Y. 'broadcast' looks like part of the fishing scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast something is to make it widely known, i.e. to inform or announce it to people.

clue.text: A little skill seen in work

indicators.note: seen in places the skill word within the word for work

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
art is a skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A modest amount of skill is visible in someone's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean to some extent or in part, not wholly.

clue.text: One follows bullet's end, one going fast

indicators.note: the end of the word bullet is its final letter

parts.note: a racer is something or someone going fast

explanation.surface: Something trailing behind a bullet as it speeds along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bullet's end' gives T; 'One follows' is a deliberately vague definition, since a tracer follows or tracks something.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracer is someone who follows or tracks down people or things, as in a tracer of lost persons.

clue.text: Strong new top on rubbish bag's lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters are raised, i.e. read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate or top
rot is nonsense or rubbish
to net something is to bag it, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A strong new lid on a bin bag is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is A1 (first-class), written as the letters AI. N + AI + ROT + NETS, lifted (reversed in a down light), gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stentorian voice is very loud and powerful, named after Stentor, the loud-voiced Greek herald at Troy.

clue.text: Roots said to provide seasonings

indicators.note: said signals that the word for roots is spoken and we write a word sounding like it

parts.note: roots are origins or sources

explanation.surface: Root vegetables are offered as flavourings.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent SOURCES and SAUCES sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauces are liquid accompaniments that add flavour to food, like other seasonings or condiments.

clue.text: A doctor's reportedly healthier anti-ageing remedy

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: reportedly means the next word is heard rather than written as spelt

parts.note: rosier means healthier-looking, with rosy cheeks

explanation.surface: A doctor claims to be healthier thanks to a youth-preserving treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic speech ROSIER sounds like ROSIA. The 's after doctor is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ambrosia was the food of the gods that kept them immortal and forever young.

clue.text: Fondled and was inclined to embrace curvy figure

indicators.note: to embrace means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to have cared to do something is to have been inclined to
ESS is the letter S, an S-shaped curve

explanation.surface: Someone stroked a curvaceous figure, feeling inclined to hug it.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress is to touch or stroke gently and lovingly, which is what fondling means.

clue.text: Blue china's overturned by husband being careless

indicators.note: by means next to, so the husband letter is placed alongside
overturned in a down light means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
china is cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A careless husband knocks over a piece of blue china.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' is cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate. SAD + PALS overturned gives SLAPDAS; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is done hastily and carelessly, without proper attention.

clue.text: Menace of hard right in time destroyed

indicators.note: in places the hard and right letters inside the time-plus-destroyed string

parts.note: eaten away means destroyed or consumed
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The danger posed by the hard right in an age of destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone is to threaten them; both verbs mean to pose a danger.

clue.text: Crossing Tiber, I arrived somewhere far away

indicators.note: the answer runs across the words, straddling them as a hidden run

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses the Tiber and ends up in a distant land.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden across 'Tiber, I arrived'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian peninsula, Spain and Portugal, is a distant region from the viewpoint of the Tiber in Rome.

clue.text: Unusually high plunge nearly leading contest

indicators.note: leading means the first piece goes in front of the second
nearly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a fall is a plunge
a set-to is a fight or contest

explanation.surface: A dramatic plunge almost leads in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto is a male voice pitched artificially above its natural range, so unusually high.

clue.text: One's sat around waiting

indicators.note: around means the word for sat is placed round the other piece

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat gives posed
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone has been sitting about, killing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Poised describes being ready and balanced, waiting to act at any moment.

clue.text: Fallen Greek character went back up

indicators.note: up in a down light means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to renege is to go back on a promise

explanation.surface: A Greek figure, once fallen, rose again.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone degenerate has declined morally, like a fallen woman or a fallen angel.

clue.text: 'Stubborner', in essence, describes American obstinacy

indicators.note: describes here means encloses, as a line describes a figure, so the answer is held within the words

explanation.surface: A word for more stubborn sums up American stubbornness.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'Stubborner, in essence'; 'in essence' looks like an instruction but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Orneriness is a US colloquial word for cantankerous stubbornness.

clue.text: Energy shown covering Queen hit precisely

indicators.note: covering means the energy word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: vim is energy or vigour
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
to bat a ball is to hit it

explanation.surface: A spirited batter plays a royal shot exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbatim means word for word, quoting exactly or precisely.

clue.text: Motor with old exhaust left roundabout

parts.note: a motor is a car
to use up is to exhaust

explanation.surface: A car with an old exhaust abandoned on a roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' looks like the traffic feature but is the British name for a fairground merry-go-round.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel is a merry-go-round, which in Britain is also called a roundabout.

clue.text: Unattached and careful with one sweetheart to finish

indicators.note: to finish means the letter is sent to the end of the word

parts.note: discreet means careful or prudent

explanation.surface: A careful single person ends up with a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one sweetheart' is one E, the heart of swEet: one of the two Es in the careful word moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate and distinct, not joined or attached to anything.

clue.text: Destroyed mice finally spread round cellar's opening

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word mice
round means the spreading word goes round the next letter

parts.note: radiated means spread outwards

indicators.note: a word's opening is its first letter

explanation.surface: Mice were wiped out as poison spread around the cellar entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Eradicated means wiped out completely, destroyed root and branch.

clue.text: Baseless financial statement Democrat changed

indicators.note: baseless in a down light means the bottom letter is removed

parts.note: the Budget is the government's annual financial statement

explanation.surface: A groundless budget from a Democrat was revised.
explanation.definitionFit: Budged means moved or shifted position, so altered or changed.

clue.text: Sure flipping bonkers, the French!

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the crazy word is reversed

parts.note: bats means crazy or bonkers
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the French are completely mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British expletive but reverses BATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means steady and secure, firm and so sure.

clue.text: Foreigners' right to inhabit outskirts of Athens

indicators.note: to inhabit means to live within, so one piece sits inside the other
outskirts are the outer edges, so the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: a lien is a legal right over another's property

explanation.surface: Outsiders claiming a right to live on the edge of Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens are people from another country, foreign nationals.

clue.text: Open up head of big fish

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Cutting open the head of a large fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject or a cask is to open it up for the first time.

clue.text: Pleading victim's encased in concrete

indicators.note: encased in means the victim word is enclosed by the concrete word

parts.note: concrete means real, actual
a butt of jokes is a victim

explanation.surface: A murder victim found buried in concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concrete' suggests the building material but means REAL; 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a counter-argument, a legal pleading in reply to a claim.

clue.text: Ship in extremities rolls

indicators.note: in places the ship letters within the extremities word

parts.note: toes are extremities of the body
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A ship rolls in severe conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosses means pitches or rolls about, as a ship does in a storm.

clue.text: Substantial hint compiler almost ruined

parts.note: a tang is a hint or trace of flavour
the setter, or compiler, refers to themself as I

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to blow a chance is to ruin it, so blew means ruined

explanation.surface: A meaningful clue that the setter nearly spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tangible is real and concrete enough to touch, hence substantial.

clue.text: Audibly grind the stuff producing grain

indicators.note: audibly means the phrase is heard, so we write what it sounds like

parts.note: to mill grain is to grind it; the stuff, the thing in question, is it

explanation.surface: Grind the substance noisily to make flour.
explanation.definitionFit: Millet is a cereal crop with small seeds, used as a grain for food and birdseed.

clue.text: Lacking guts, novice evaded love scenes as 'unnecessary'

indicators.note: lacking guts means the insides are removed, leaving the outer letters of each word

explanation.surface: A timid novice avoided the romantic scenes as superfluous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking guts' reads as cowardice but empties four words, leaving NE ED LE SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means not needed, superfluous or unnecessary.
